summary: 19-year-old man with a silent chest, exhaustion and drowsiness: SpO₂ 90 %, HR 132, BP 104/62, PEF unrecordable. BTS/SIGN life-threatening features: critical care, magnesium.

inputs.hpi: Brought in by his mother from the waiting room. Brittle asthma with a previous ICU admission. Worsening since last night despite repeated inhaler use. Now too breathless to talk, getting drowsy.

exam.general: Exhausted, drowsy, cyanosed lips, unable to speak.
exam.respiratory: Silent chest, poor respiratory effort, RR 30.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Life-threatening asthma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Life-threatening asthma (silent chest, SpO2 90%, exhaustion, drowsy): 999, oxygen, nebulised salbutamol and ipratropium, IV magnesium, critical care.

guideline.name: BTS/SIGN 158 - British guideline on the management of asthma
guideline.section: Section 9 acute asthma in adults: acute severe = PEF 33-50% best/predicted, RR >=25/min, HR >=110/min or inability to complete sentences; life-threatening = PEF <33%, SpO2 <92%, silent chest, cyanosis, poor respiratory effort, arrhythmia, exhaustion, altered consciousness, hypotension; oxygen to SpO2 94-98%, high-dose inhaled beta2 agonist, ipratropium in severe/life-threatening, prednisolone 40-50 mg, IV magnesium sulphate for severe asthma not responding; Section 12 pregnancy: treat as in non-pregnant patients, do not withhold steroids, fetal monitoring in acute severe asthma
guideline.citation: British Thoracic Society / Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. SIGN 158. Edinburgh: SIGN; 2019.

guideline.name: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) - Global strategy for asthma management and prevention
guideline.section: Management of worsening asthma and exacerbations: assess severity; SABA (+ ipratropium in severe), controlled oxygen, systemic corticosteroids; transfer to acute care if features of severe or life-threatening exacerbation
guideline.citation: Global Initiative for Asthma. GINA report 2024. www.ginasthma.org.
